title: Rank structure of the Hankel matrix of a formal Laurent series and its best approximation denominators
author: Roswitha Hofer
work: Variants of the Littlewood conjecture, their connection to uniformly distributed sequences, and the exact order of the discrepancy of van der Corput--Kronecker-type sequences
difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is not a formal consequence of the definitions of the digital method that precede it. Even with the continued fraction machinery of F_p((X^{-1})) - the convergents P_h/Q_h, the degree identities deg(theta - P_h/Q_h) = -d_h - d_{h+1} and the best-approximation property of the intermediate denominators - supplied as context, the author has to translate regularity of the upper-left m x m submatrix of the Hankel matrix into a single exact statement about the degree of the fractional part of a polynomial multiple of theta, that is, into the existence of a non-zero polynomial of degree below m whose product with theta has fractional part of degree below -m, and then to characterise exactly which m admit such a polynomial: precisely the degrees d_h of the best approximation denominators, which requires using the best-approximation property in both directions, for m = d_h to prove linear independence of the columns and for d_{h-1} < m < d_h to exhibit the explicit dependence through Q_{h-1}. Turning a rank condition on an infinite Hankel matrix into a complete description of its regular principal submatrices is a research-level argument in Diophantine approximation over function fields, above ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in number theory.
